LAM.1.1-2.text: Jerusalem is lonely and has no comforter

LAM.1.3-3.text: Judah is in exile and finds no rest

LAM.1.4-5.text: Zion mourns, and her children are taken captive

LAM.1.6-6.text: The splendor of Zion is gone and her princes are weak

LAM.1.7-7.text: Jerusalem remembers her treasures while enemies laugh

LAM.1.8-9.text: Jerusalem sinned and is now despised

LAM.1.10-10.text: Enemies take treasures and enter the sanctuary

LAM.1.11-12.text: Jerusalem asks the LORD to see her great sorrow

LAM.1.13-14.text: The LORD’s hand has broken Jerusalem’s strength

LAM.1.15-15.text: The Lord has crushed Judah’s warriors like grapes

LAM.1.16-17.text: Jerusalem weeps because no one comforts her

LAM.1.18-19.text: Jerusalem admits her rebellion and asks all to look

LAM.1.20-20.text: Jerusalem asks the LORD to see her distress

LAM.1.21-22.text: Jerusalem asks the LORD to punish her enemies

LAM.2.1-2.text: The Lord in anger destroys Jerusalem’s dwellings

LAM.2.3-4.text: The Lord acts like an enemy against Israel

LAM.2.5-6.text: The Lord destroys his meeting place and ends the feasts

LAM.2.7-7.text: The Lord rejects his altar and sanctuary

LAM.2.8-9.text: The LORD destroys Zion’s walls and gates

LAM.2.10-10.text: Elders and young women of Jerusalem mourn

LAM.2.11-12.text: The writer weeps for the children fainting from hunger

LAM.2.13-14.text: Jerusalem’s wound is deep, and false prophets deceived her

LAM.2.17-17.text: The LORD did what he planned against Jerusalem

LAM.2.18-19.text: Jerusalem is told to cry to the Lord day and night

LAM.2.20-20.text: Jerusalem asks the LORD to see her terrible suffering

LAM.2.21-22.text: Young and old die on the day of the LORD’s anger

LAM.3.1-4.text: God’s anger has brought great suffering to the writer

LAM.3.5-8.text: God has shut the writer in darkness and ignores his prayer

LAM.3.9-11.text: God blocks the writer’s path like a bear or lion

LAM.3.12-15.text: God makes the writer a target and a laughingstock

LAM.3.16-18.text: The writer feels his strength and hope have perished

LAM.3.19-21.text: The writer remembers his suffering, yet has hope

LAM.3.22-24.text: The LORD’s mercies are new every morning

LAM.3.25-29.text: It is good to wait quietly for the LORD

LAM.3.30-33.text: The Lord will not reject his people forever

LAM.3.34-36.text: The Lord does not approve of injustice

LAM.3.37-39.text: Everything comes from God, so people should not complain

LAM.3.40-43.text: The people turn back to the LORD and confess sin

LAM.3.44-47.text: God blocks prayers, and enemies bring ruin to the people

LAM.3.48-50.text: The prophet weeps for the destruction of his people

LAM.3.51-54.text: Enemies hunt the prophet and throw him into a pit

LAM.3.55-57.text: The prophet calls to the LORD, who comes near

LAM.3.58-61.text: The prophet asks the LORD to defend him against enemies

LAM.3.62-63.text: Enemies slander and mock the prophet all day

LAM.3.64-66.text: The prophet asks the LORD to punish his enemies

LAM.4.1-2.text: Zion’s people, once precious, are now like clay jars

LAM.4.3-3.text: Mothers in Zion are more cruel than jackals

LAM.4.4-5.text: Children go hungry and the once rich are poor

LAM.4.6-6.text: Zion is punished more than Sodom was

LAM.4.7-8.text: Once-healthy leaders now look dark and shriveled

LAM.4.9-10.text: Hunger is so bad that mothers cook children

LAM.4.11-11.text: The LORD pours out his anger and burns Zion

LAM.4.12-13.text: Jerusalem falls for the sins of prophets and priests

LAM.4.14-15.text: Prophets and priests wander blind and are driven away

LAM.4.16-16.text: The LORD scatters the people, and priests get no honor

LAM.4.17-18.text: The people wait in vain for help while enemies hunt

LAM.4.19-20.text: Enemies chase the people and capture the king

LAM.4.21-22.text: Edom will be punished, but Zion’s punishment is complete

LAM.5.1-4.text: The people ask the LORD to remember what happened

LAM.5.5-7.text: The people are weary and suffer for fathers’ sins

LAM.5.8-10.text: Slaves rule the people, and food is hard to find

LAM.5.11-12.text: Women are abused and leaders are shamed in Judah

LAM.5.13-14.text: Young men and boys work hard, and joy has stopped

LAM.5.15-16.text: Joy turns to mourning, and the people admit sin

LAM.5.17-18.text: The people grow faint over the ruined Mount Zion

LAM.5.19-22.text: The people ask the LORD to restore the nation
